subject: radiology
title: Uterine prostate and bariatric embolisation

steps.tx: Uterine artery embolisation is a treatment for fibroid symptoms while the uterus stays in place afterwards. A patient with **symptomatic fibroids** reports heavy periods, pelvic pressure and bulk that disturb daily life repeatedly. Particles block both uterine arteries and the **fibroid** then shrinks over the following months without open surgery. Emergency embolisation also controls **postpartum haemorrhage** when drugs and balloon tamponade fail to stop the bleeding. Adenomyosis responds only partly, so pain eases rather than disappears after treatment in many patients.
steps.say: Uterine artery embolisation is a treatment for fibroid symptoms while the uterus stays in place afterwards. A patient with troublesome fibroids has heavy periods and pelvic pressure that disturb daily life. Particles block both uterine arteries and the fibroid then shrinks over the following months. Emergency embolisation also controls bleeding after delivery when drugs and balloon treatment fail completely. Adenomyosis is different because pain eases only partly rather than disappears after treatment in many patients.

steps.tx: This pelvic angiogram is helpful because it shows a microcatheter that sits inside a tortuous **uterine artery** on one side of the pelvis. Contrast fills a dense **fibroid blush**, which marks the hypervascular fibroid that drinks most of the uterine flow. A faint **ovarian collateral** also appears near the top, and that vessel can keep a fibroid alive after uterine blockage. The image matters for the exam because bilateral treatment and collateral awareness decide success. A trainee who spots the blush can understand why particles shrink the fibroid.
steps.say: This pelvic angiogram is helpful because it shows a microcatheter that sits inside a markedly tortuous uterine artery. Contrast fills a dense blush that marks the hypervascular fibroid drinking most of the flow. A faint collateral vessel also appears near the top and that vessel can sustain the fibroid. Bilateral treatment and collateral awareness decide success in uterine embolisation for fibroids. A trainee who spots the blush can understand why particles shrink the fibroid over months.

steps.tx: Prostate artery embolisation gives an option when surgery feels too risky or unwanted for urinary symptoms. The procedure suits a man with **lower urinary tract symptoms** from benign enlargement who cannot undergo or refuses resection. Treatment preserves **sexual function** including ejaculation better than resection does in comparative follow up studies. A **large gland** that measures over 80 mL often responds well when tablets have already failed. Retention with a catheter can resolve in selected cases, while proven cancer needs oncology care instead of embolisation.
steps.say: Prostate artery embolisation gives an option when surgery feels too risky or unwanted for symptoms. The procedure is suitable for a man with urinary symptoms from benign enlargement who refuses resection surgery. Treatment preserves sexual function including ejaculation better than resection does during later follow up. A large gland often responds well when tablets have already failed for that patient. Retention with a catheter can resolve in selected cases while proven cancer needs oncology care.

steps.tx: Technique decides safety in selective embolisation, and the operator treats both sides in uterus and prostate work. **Bilateral embolisation** matters because a single sided treatment invites collateral flow and later rebleeding from the other side. **Cone beam CT** during the case maps each feeder and excludes dangerous links toward bladder, rectum or penis. **Non target embolisation** injures skin, bladder or rectum, so the operator keeps the catheter tip distal and secure. Pain peaks within hours after the procedure and the team controls pain with a protocol and anti sickness drugs.
steps.say: Technique decides safety in selective embolisation and the operator treats both sides in pelvic work. Bilateral treatment matters because a single sided treatment invites collateral flow and later rebleeding. Cone beam imaging during the case maps each feeder and excludes dangerous links toward nearby organs. Particles that stray into skin or bladder or rectum cause injury so the tip stays distal. Pain peaks within hours after the procedure and the team controls pain with a clear protocol.

steps.tx: Newer embolisation targets remain investigational, and the examiner expects caution rather than enthusiasm for frontier work. **Left gastric artery embolisation** aims at hunger signalling and early studies show weight signals that need confirmation. The method stays **research only** outside a formal protocol because long term benefit remains unproven for routine care. Genicular embolisation for knee pain and haemorrhoidal embolisation through rectal branches suit only selected patients today. Every frontier indication needs **trial enrolment** or ethics approval before the team offers the procedure to anyone.
